A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLHF Game mechanism-design work. All 24 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including proof Appendices A and B, support reliable comparison across the changed pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical models, theoretical results, and proofs, including in both appendices. It contains no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 contains theoretical results and proof appendices but no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: The RLHF Game formulation, regularized social-welfare objective, affine-maximizer payment rule, and two practical payment approximations in Section 6 are retained.

E1.justification: Neither version uses concrete datasets or tasks for original training or evaluation. The discussed applications and references to empirical research are unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. The other methods discussed in Sections 1 and 5 remain related-work references.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. Discussions of regularization, valuation sampling, and approximate training remain theoretical and unchanged.

E4.justification: No empirical ablations, sensitivity tests, or case studies are added or removed. The bounded-error analysis in Section 4.2 and its appendix proofs are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The valuation-noise assumptions and theoretical error bounds are unchanged.

E6.justification: Neither version contains measured performance results, and no result entries are added, removed, or corrected. The reported theoretical findings are retained.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, and derivations in Sections 2–4 and Appendices A–B match. This includes the payment-necessity, DSIC/IR, payment-equivalence, and approximate-DSIC results and their proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning payment necessity, incentive compatibility, payment equivalence, revenue maximization, and robustness to noisy preferences.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2 and 6 retain the same interpretations of valuation noise, computational-cost versus incentive-compatibility tradeoffs, applicability conditions, and future directions.

D1.justification: Section 6 retains the same checkpoint-reuse and reduced-iteration payment approximations. No implementation settings, hardware details, or code/data access information are added or revised.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained, including the comparisons with Duetting et al. and Soumalias et al. The wording refinement in Section 5 does not substantively change the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: Section 5 changes 'rationality' to 'economic rationality.' The remaining prose, section sequence, and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout, with different fonts, text widths and spacing, a redesigned title/author block without horizontal rules, blue citation and cross-reference styling, and reflowed equations across the main text and appendices. Neither version contains figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 retains the same scientific arguments, assumptions, and complete proofs. Its extensive reformatting and the small 'economic rationality' wording refinement leave the paper substantively equivalent in clarity, scientific support, and reproducibility; both layouts remain readable.
